To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) plasma concentrations of adenosine are significantly higher in conscious SHR compared to age- and sex-matched normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats and that 2) the higher plasma adenosine concentration in SHR is not due to a greater rate of adenosine release from the kidney, but rather is a reflection of a lower rate of adenosinal metabolism in the kidney.

plasma adenosine levels were significantly elevated in conscious, unrestrained SHR as compared to age-matched control Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats, and that the elevation in plasma adenosine was associated with increased plasma levels of epinephrine and norepinephrine.

plasma levels of adenosinc are elevated in SHR compared with Wistar Kyoto (WKY) rats, that the increase is due to a decrease in the rate of clearance, that the rate of production is unchanged, that the increase in plasma adenosine is associated with increased renal blood flow, and that the increase in renal plasma flow is associated with increased sodium and water excretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the determination of adenosine in the plasma of conscious, freely-moving rats.
the role of adenosin in the cardiovascular regulation of spontaneously hypertensive rats and the effect of adenosine on the renal function.
the role of adenosines in cardiovascular regulation and in the pathophysiology of hypertension.

adenosine concentrations are increased in plasma of SHR, but the increase is not due to an alteration in renal function.
the results indicate that adenosine is a candidate substance for the regulation of cardiovascular homeostasis in conscious SHR.
